reflections.title: The Bitter Cry of a Lost Blessing

reflect.text: Esau let out a loud, bitter cry when he discovered the blessing was gone. Long before this day, he had yielded to a passing physical craving and traded away his birthright. As F. B. Meyer points out, choices made in such moments can cast a shadow that cannot be undone. Esau longed for the blessing afterward, but his tears could not turn back the clock or change the outcome.

This sad moment warns us to watch and pray so sudden desires do not overwhelm us. We need to remember four great truths. First, we were once dead in our sins, and we must not return to that spiritual decay. Second, Christ died for our sins as our representative, showing how terrible sin is by paying its awful cost. Third, we died with Jesus and were raised into His new life of righteousness.

Finally, we are called to reckon ourselves dead to sin. The closer we live to God, the quicker we will spot temptation. We can close every door against evil, count ourselves as Meyer says "not at home" to sin, and offer ourselves completely to God.

questions: What momentary cravings or sudden desires do you need God to guard you against today?
How can remembering Christ's death on the cross help you shut the door against temptation?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for Jesus, who paid the heavy price for my sins and gave me new life. Keep me watchful in prayer so I do not yield to sudden temptations that bring regret. Help me to close my heart against evil and offer every part of my life to Your service. Amen.
